description: Hook points of anything run by aos-loop whose loop.json wires them (the templates wire them through aos-hook fire --stop-on-nonzero): after_start / after_stop (on_start / on_stop) and before_run / after_run (on_before_run / on_after_run). The event JSON has only event, hook and stack; what the loop knows comes in the handler's environment (AOS_LOOP_*). Exit codes reach aos-loop as they are: a non-zero code stops the loop at all four points, except 10 at before_run, which skips that run.

after_start.description: the loop started, before the first run of its body (loop.json on_start; also after a wake or an auto_restart, not after a hard kill)

stack.description: the stack of the program the loop runs (the handler's own AOS_STACK is STACK/hookeds/NAME/)

after_start.if_failed: the loop stops: the body never runs, after_stop still fires

after_stop.description: the loop is about to exit (loop.json on_stop: stop, sleep, remove, shutdown, a failing run; not after a hard kill)

environment.AOS_LOOP_CODE: the code the loop exits with
environment.AOS_LOOP_SIGNAL: the signal it got, or empty
environment.AOS_LOOP_CAUSE: stop, sleep, remove, shutdown, stuck, signal, max, body_exit or error; empty when not known

after_stop.if_failed: the loop exits with the hook's code when it would have exited 0; when it already exits with another code, that code stays and the failure is one warning

before_run.description: before each run of the loop body, after the pause check and the wait for interval_ms
before_run.notes: an fsm body's state about to run is in STACK/stage.txt (missing on the first run: the table's start state)
before_run.if_blocked: exit 10: the loop skips this run (the body does not run, the run is not counted, after_run does not fire) and asks again after interval_ms
before_run.if_failed: the loop stops, as after a failing run; the body does not run

after_run.description: after each run of the loop body, whatever its exit code (not when the body could not start, not when the loop got a signal)

environment.AOS_LOOP_RUNS: which run this was (the number before_run got)
environment.AOS_LOOP_RUN_SIGNAL: the signal that ended the body, or empty

after_run.notes: an fsm body's state now (the next one after a taken step) is in STACK/stage.txt
after_run.if_failed: any non-zero code, 10 too: the loop stops with that code when the body exited 0; when the body itself ends the loop, the body's result counts and the failure is one warning
